For the reviewer\n\n**Outcome:** two tests of `packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox` no longer fail when a launch's waits on the wall clock run past a boot timeout of 1 s or 2 s on a slow machine. Their launches must succeed, so the rig now gives those waits a boot timeout as long as the test binary's deadline allows, and each wait ends on the event it waits for. The change is test-only.\n\n### `TestAnIssuePodOfTheEarlierLayoutIsStaleForEveryRoleAndReplacedByTheNextLaunch` (`one_container_test.go`)\n\nIt failed in `daemon-go / daemon-go (leg 1)` of CI run [45752994928](https://github.com/cybermonklabs/legion/actions/runs/45752994928/job/139685386402) (#4296's `2be8b3588d`, which changes no file of this package), after 4.13 s:\n\n`one_container_test.go:384: Resume the tester: launch legion-legion-legion-208-tester: wait out its previous pod: timed out after 2s waiting for the pod of sandbox legion-legion-legion-208 to be gone`\n\n**Cause.** The launch replaces the earlier pod, and `awaitPodGone` (`relaunch.go:1203`) waits until the pod is gone, bounded by the runtime's boot timeout. The product does not set that 2 s: `testOptions()` (`rig_test.go:98`) sets `BootTimeout: 2 * time.Second`, and in production the bound is `worker_boot_timeout_seconds`. In the rig, the pod's deletion is asynchronous: the controller stand-in (`rig.control`, a 5 ms ticker) marks the pod terminating on one tick, deletes it on a later tick, and the pod informer then delivers the delete. A loaded runner (eight tests of this package at once, beside the three other packages of leg 1) can hold that chain past 2 s.\n\n**Fix.** A rig option, `withWaitsToTheDeadline()` (`rig_test.go`), sets the boot timeout to `testwait.Remaining(t)`: what is left of the test binary's deadline when the rig is made, less 30 s. `docs/testing.md` names `Remaining` for a wait that is not the test's subject. The test uses it. Each of the launch's waits ends on an event the rig always brings: the controller deletes the old pod and makes a new one, and the fake launchers connect to the new pod. On the wall clock each wait also checks again every `recheckInterval`, so no wait depends on an event that may never come. The timeout is at most a day: under `-timeout 0`, `Remaining` is about 36 years, and `launchBound`, about ten boot timeouts, would overflow a `time.Duration`.\n\n### `TestAStartWhoseAnswerIsDelayedPastItsDeadlineIsStoppedBeforeResumeReturns` (`relaunch_test.go`)\n\nIts subtest `on_the_same_pod_as_its_previous_locator` failed in `daemon-go / daemon-go (leg 1)` of CI run 45755173281, at #4186's `7555f1a1f5`, with `relaunch_test.go:1980: no generation-2 Start`. #4186 does not touch the test, and its branch does not have main's #5565. The cause was the start deadline: 1 s of wall clock passed before the Start was written, so the launcher never received it. Main's #5565 (`1a5f6505bd`) already fixed that cause: the start deadline now runs on a fake clock, and the test moves the clock only once the launcher holds the Start. The verification below shows it: with the Start held 1.5 s before its write, main before #5565 fails 3 of 3 with CI's text, and main after it passes 3 of 3.\n\nThis PR fixes the two waits of the test that #5565 left on the wall clock, still under the test's 1 s boot timeout:\n\n- The first spawn (`awaitNewPod`, `awaitRoleLauncher`). With the rig's pod creation held 1.5 s, main fails: `spawn legion-legion-legion-208-tester: launch legion-legion-legion-208-tester: wait for its new pod: timed out after 1s …`.\n- The Stop of the issued generation (`stopIssuedChild`, bounded by the boot timeout plus the termination grace). With the Stop's write held 1.5 s, the write fails, `requestSession` closes the launcher's connection, and the launcher never receives the Stop the test is about. Main fails: `relaunch_test.go:2025: no generation-2 Stop before the test binary's deadline`.\n\nThe test now uses `withWaitsToTheDeadline()` too. The fake-clock advance (`fc.Advance(g.opts.BootTimeout + g.opts.TerminationGrace)`) reads the options, so it moves past the new start deadline. The 50 ms termination grace override is removed: its purpose was a short start deadline on the wall clock, which #5565 removed.\n\nBoth tests still call `t.Parallel()`.\n\n## Verification\n\n**Forced records** (the `c-fix-at-cause` check, forced mode, at this head `10fa4ab93e`, `BASE` the merge base `fce9729504`, `CI_JOB` `daemon-go / daemon-go (leg 1)`, `CI_STEP` \"Test the Go daemon\"; `internal/runtime/sandbox` is in daemon-go leg 1 of `.github/go-legs.yaml`):\n\n1. The first row, forcing `podgone`. The second row, forcing `residual`. Run 07:17:42Z to 07:42:25Z.\n   - Check c-fix-at-cause (before_merge): pass at 10fa4ab93e115336d165db3ee2997567d1532bc0, recorded by implementer. forced: base failed 3 of 3, head passed 3 of 3, latest CI run of daemon-go /…\n\nCI at this head: run [45773525968](https://github.com/cybermonklabs/legion/actions/runs/45773525968). Its `daemon-go / daemon-go (leg 1)` (job 139752068108) passed, with `ok github.com/sjawhar/legion/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox 191.432s`. The pull request carried the label `lane:daemon_go_tests` for this run.\n\n### Forcing kit\n\nEach run is one builds Job (gVisor, 4 CPU) at the checkout's commit, fetched by SHA from GitHub. The Job adds one test file and inserts one line that calls it in the row's own test function. No line is removed. A run exits 0 when the row prints its own `--- PASS` line and the plant fired, 1 when the row prints its own `--- FAIL` line with the forcing's failure text and the plant fired, and 2 in all other cases.\n\n- `podgone` (the first row): after the test's `newRig` line, the rig's controller holds each pod it deletes terminating for 3 s (`g.suspendDelay`). The plant prints `PLANT fired: pod … is still terminating …ms after its deletion began` once the pod has been terminating 100 ms. The expected failure text is CI's.\n- `residual` (the second row's subtest `on_the_same_pod_as_its_previous_locator`): two runs in one Job, each with one plant. `spawn`, before the test's `spec := workerSpec(t)` line: the rig's controller makes no pod for 1.5 s (`g.hold`); expected failure text `wait for its new pod: timed out after 1s`. `stop`, after the test's `delayed.written()` line: the runtime's next frame to the launcher, the Stop of generation 2, is held 1.5 s inside its write (a writer that wraps the session's connection); expected failure text `no generation-2 Stop`. That run uses `-timeout 3m`, because the base fails at the Stop helper's give-up, 30 s before the binary's deadline. `residual` exits 0 only when both runs exit 0, and 1 only when both exit 1.\n- `start` (evidence for #5565, not a record of this PR): after the test's first `g.spawn`, `launchers.beforeStart` holds each later Start 1.5 s before its write. The expected failure text is CI's (`no generation-2 Start`).\n\nThe kit's controls: a run with no `go test` output (a stub `go`) printed \"printed neither its PASS nor its FAIL line: unknown\" and exited 2. A test file without the plant's anchor printed \"the anchor … is not in …\" and exited 2. An earlier form of the `stop` plant held the session's lock instead. Main passed under it, because the lock also held the Start's own return, so the Stop's wait began after the hold. The plant was replaced with the write hold, under which main fails.\n\n### #5565's fix of the second row's CI cause (the `start` forcing)\n\n- Main before #5565, `5a972e7d37` (runs started 2026-11-26 05:35:52Z, 07:05:19Z and 07:05:24Z): 3 of 3 failed with `no generation-2 Start`. The plant printed `PLANT released: … (its context: context deadline exceeded)`.\n- Main after #5565, `fce9729504` (runs started 06:35:03Z, 07:05:29Z and 07:05:34Z): 3 of 3 passed, with the plant fired.\n\n### Under load, unforced\n\nAt main `5a972e7d37`, with `-race`, 8 busy loops on the pod's 4 CPUs and `-count=40` per row, the first row passed 40 of 40 and the second row's subtest passed 40 of 40. The load alone did not reproduce either failure. The forced runs reproduce each failure with its CI text.\n\nLocal checks at this head: `gofmt -l internal/runtime/sandbox/` printed nothing, `go vet ./internal/runtime/sandbox/` exited 0, and `merged_vet.py 5641` (this head merged with main and the 15 queued pull requests ahead of it) printed `VET CLEAN: 3 packages of the merged the clustered hub's scrape keeps no JetStream consumer series","user":{"login":"sjawhar-agent[bot]","id":329211056,"node_id":"BOT_kgDOE59csA","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/5074378?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/sjawhar-agent%5Bbot%5D","html_url":"https://github.com/apps/sjawhar-agent","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/sjawhar-agent%5Bbot%5D/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/sjawhar-agent%5Bbot%5D/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/sjawhar-agent%5Bbot%5D/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/sjawhar-agent%5Bbot%5D/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/sjawhar-agent%5Bbot%5D/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/sjawhar-agent%5Bbot%5D/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/sjawhar-agent%5Bbot%5D/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/sjawhar-agent%5Bbot%5D/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/sjawhar-agent%5Bbot%5D/received_events","type":"Bot","user_view_type":"public","site_admin":false},"body":"## What was wrong\n\nEach clustered hub pod runs prometheus-nats-exporter with the nats chart's arguments, `-jsz=all` among them. That reads every JetStream consumer and serves up to ten series for each one, labelled with the consumer's name and description: eight always, and two more once the consumer has delivered and been acknowledged (`collector/jsz.go:111-115`, `:430-431` and `:625-640` at exporter 0.20.2). Google Managed Prometheus scrapes them through the hub's PodMonitoring and keeps them, so every holder of `monitoring.timeSeries.list` in the project can read every consumer's name. A Legion daemon's consumer carries its daemon's name, a private project's daemon's among them.\n\nThe deployment repository's main now has the `hub-stream-consumers` alert. It reads `nats_consumer_num_pending` by `consumer_name`. It must move to `nats_stream_consumer_count` before any deployment pins the envoy-infra release that contains this rule; plan task t-f-21 carries that dependency. The rule works forward only. Managed Prometheus retains consumer series stored before the apply. No private project is live yet, so no stored consumer series holds private-project text.\n\n## The change\n\nThe hub's PodMonitoring gets one metric relabeling rule: drop every series whose name matches `nats_consumer_.+`. It applies on every render, with `privateProjects` and without. The exporter keeps the chart's arguments.\n\nThe first design set the exporter's arguments to `-jsz=streams`. That serves no consumer series. It also reads `/jsz?streams=true` with no `config=true` (`collector/jsz.go:432-433`; nats-server v2.15.1 `server/monitor.go:3187` sends a stream's configuration only with it). So the exporter would stop serving `nats_stream_limit_bytes` and `nats_stream_limit_messages` (`collector/jsz.go:540-543`). A stream's byte-limit alert divides by `nats_stream_limit_bytes`, and a PromQL condition with no series never fires. Measured against nats-server 2.15.1, with a consumer that had delivered nothing: `-jsz=all` served `nats_stream_limit_bytes` and 8 consumer series; `-jsz=streams` served neither.\n\nThe PodMonitoring is the exporter's only scraper. The hub's NetworkPolicy admits the exporter's port, 7777, only from the Managed Prometheus namespaces. No other PodMonitoring, ClusterPodMonitoring, ServiceMonitor or Datadog annotation selects the hub's pods.\n\n## Merging main\n\nMain is merged in at 930a534829. One file conflicted: `gcp/clusteredhub_kube.go`. Main (#4668) moved the hub pods' NetworkPolicy above the nats chart, so that with `privateProjects` the chart waits on the policy. The resolution keeps main's placement, and this branch's comment and drop rule on the PodMonitoring. Every other file merged without a conflict. Main's own changes to the production render's golden file since this branch's first head touch only permission lines in `auth.conf`, never a PodMonitoring.\n\n## Rollout\n\nThe merge starts the envoy-infra release workflow, which cuts a plugin release. No deployment may pin that release until the deployment repository moves `hub-stream-consumers` to `nats_stream_consumer_count`. Then the apply updates one PodMonitoring. The pods do not roll, because the chart's values do not change. The rule affects new scrapes only; consumer series stored before the apply remain through Managed Prometheus's retention.\n\n## Tests\n\nA new live test, tagged `natslive`, renders the chart with helm v3.20.2 from the vendored archive and reads the exporter's arguments from that render. It runs prometheus-nats-exporter 0.20.2 with those arguments against a nats-server. The server holds a stream with a byte limit and a durable consumer that has delivered and acknowledged one message. The test then applies the PodMonitoring's rule, as the component registers it, to every series one scrape serves. It does this for a hub with `privateProjects` and for one without. Without the rule, all ten `nats_consumer_*` families must name the consumer, which shows the test can see them. With the rule, no kept series may carry the consumer's name or description in any label, and every other series must stay. When a series that names the consumer is kept, the test fails naming the PodMonitoring (`envoy/envoy-nats`) and that series.\n\nThe test applies the rule with a small Go copy of the collectors' drop and keep semantics. It joins the source labels with `;` and anchors the regex at both ends, as Google's Prometheus fork does, which Managed Prometheus's collectors run (v2.53.5-gmp.7 in GKE; `model/relabel/relabel.go:34`, `:173-175` and `:251-261` at 3f3316d7cf6f). The model accepts only `action`, `sourceLabels` and `regex`, and `sourceLabels` must be exactly `[__name__]`: it reads exporter labels, not target labels Managed Prometheus adds after scraping. The proof below runs the real engines on the same rule.\n\nResults at this head, 7a7be4cd41, run with `go test -count=1` from `packages/envoy/infra` on Go 1.27.3:\n\n| Run | Result |\n|---|---|\n| `gofmt -l .` and `go vet -tags pulumilive,natslive ./...` | `gofmt` printed nothing; `go vet` exited 0 |\n| `go test -count=1 ./...` | every package `ok`, including `github.com/sjawhar/envoy/infra/gcp` |\n| `-run '^(TestProductionRender\\|TestClusteredNatsHubPodMonitoring)$' ./gcp/` | both passed |\n| `-tags natslive -run '^TestTheHubsScrapeKeepsNoConsumerSeriesOnEveryRender$' -v ./gcp/` | both rows passed. Without `privateProjects`: served 170, dropped 10 consumer series and kept 160. With it: served 170, dropped 10 and kept 160. `nats_stream_limit_bytes` and `nats_stream_last_seq` were kept in both. |\n| The same, with the drop rule removed from `gcp/clusteredhub_kube.go` (control) | both rows failed: the PodMonitoring `envoy/envoy-nats` kept 10 consumer series. `TestClusteredNatsHubPodMonitoring` and `TestProductionRender` failed too. |\n| The same, with `sourceLabels: [job]` instead of `[__name__]` (control) | both rows failed before the model applied the rule: `the model has only the exporter's metric name, not target labels Managed Prometheus adds`. `TestMetricNameSourceLabels` also fails if its exact source-label guard accepts `job`. |\n| The same, without `-tags natslive` (control) | no test ran: 0 `--- PASS` lines for the test |\n| `-tags natslive -run '^(TestClusteredNatsHubChart\\|TestClusteredNatsHubCluster)$' -v ./gcp/` at the preceding head | both passed. The cluster test's exporter step logged every `nats_stream_*` series of its three-copy stream, `nats_stream_limit_bytes` among them. |\n\nThe production render's golden file changes only by the two PodMonitorings' new `metricRelabeling` entries (the shapes with and without tailnet). The chart's values are unchanged.\n\n## Verification\n\nA second agent, which did not write the first implementation, ran four scenarios at 9d5a8d85bc. Since then, the branch merged main; the live test now names the PodMonitoring that keeps a consumer series; and the model now refuses source labels other than `[__name__]`. The PodMonitoring the component registers and the exporter's rendered arguments are the same as in that evidence: the golden file's PodMonitoring entries did not change across the merge, and the live test reads the rendered arguments.\n\n- **Managed Prometheus's admission and translation: RAN.** A driver program created the PodMonitoring the component registers, for a hub with `privateProjects` and one without, on a real kube-apiserver 1.36.2 (envtest) with the operator's CRD. It then called the operator's own conversion to a Prometheus scrape config, with prometheus-engine v0.19.4 and with v0.18.2-rc.2 (the GKE cluster runs operator v0.18.2-gke.1). Both gave `ADMISSION: created` and `1 metric_relabel_configs: source_labels: [__name__], regex: nats_consumer_.+, action: drop`. The merge base gives 0. Controls: a `replace` onto `project_id` or `namespace` and a `labelmap` were refused at admission. A `labeldrop` of `namespace` and an unbalanced regex were refused at conversion.\n- **The real engines on the real exporter: RAN.** nats-server 2.15.1 held a stream with a 1 MiB byte limit and a durable consumer that had acknowledged one message. Exporter 0.20.2 ran with the chart's rendered arguments. Upstream Prometheus (v0.315.1) and the collectors' fork (2.53.5-gmp.8) each scraped it with the converted rule (`hub`) and without it (`hub-no-rule`). Both gave `count by (job) ({__name__=~\"nats_consumer_.+\"}) → hub-no-rule 10` with no `hub` row, and `nats_stream_limit_bytes → hub 1048576, hub-no-rule 1048576`. `scrape_samples_scraped / post_metric_relabeling` was `hub 171/161` and `hub-no-rule 171/171`. The series `hub` lost are exactly the ten consumer series. The fork also exported to a recording stand-in for Cloud Monitoring: records naming the consumer, `390 hub-no-rule` only. A third job scraped an exporter run with `-jsz=streams`. It served no consumer series and no `nats_stream_limit_bytes` either.\n- **The chart's objects at the merge base and at the head: RAN.** The values the component gives the chart are byte-identical at both (sha256 `8f7a790c…` without `privateProjects`, `d2bfc6a7…` with it). `helm template` of the vendored archive on each gives `diff` exit 0 for both. Across every registration, the base and the head differ only by the nine `metricRelabeling` lines. Control: `diskSizeGb` 12 through the same path changed the values, the render (`storage: 10Gi→12Gi`) and the registrations.\n- **The committed tests at this head: RAN.** The new live test passed in both rows, `TestMetricNameSourceLabels` passed, and the unit tests named above passed.\n\nRead-only reads of the GKE cluster showed two things. No admission webhook covers PodMonitorings, so the CRD's schema and rules are the whole admission. The live hub's PodMonitoring holds no rule yet. After the release pin and apply, `nats_consumer_delivered_consumer_seq` should return no series, and `nats_stream_limit_bytes` should still return the hub's streams.\n","labels":[{"id":13187516720,"node_id":"LA_kwDORFy7ds8AAAADEgmJMA","url":"https://api.github.com/repos/cybermonklabs/legion/labels/lane:envoy_infra_go","name":"lane:envoy_infra_go","description":"Runs The daemon checks the ancestor and the root's structure (a view on the ancestor's requirements) and opens the step, or holds it pending on the ancestor's open approval request. Each case it refuses has a code of its own, and a refused call records nothing. The engine reads the ancestor again inside the registration's transaction, so a sign-off that committed since the API's read refuses it, and neither the pending-basis seed nor the person's approval as a live event opens a step on an accepted or unlabelled ancestor.\n- A step rests on every ancestor a basis opened it on in the generation (`rests_on` is a list), a re-registration of the same step on the same basis keeps the moment it opened, and the registration's fact id names how many times the step's basis changed (`design_gates.basis_moves`, `record.DesignGate.BasisMoves`), so a sequence such as pending, no basis, pending at one sequence is three facts.\n- The root's Dispatch issue gets one message whose first line is `Design gate opened on an ancestor's approval.`. The state, `read_record` and the catch-up name the basis (`open_on_basis`, `pending_on_basis`), and each root says whether its tree runs (`treeRuns`). An older plugin is served a body it reads.\n- A step pending on an ancestor's open approval request opens or ends only on what Dispatch shows now. Every event of the ancestor's document, of its approval request or of its issue that can change the wait queues the step's pending-basis seed, which reads Dispatch for that registration's wait and is judged by one verdict (`judgeBasisRead`): the person's approval of the version opens the step; a changes request, a newer version, the request closed with no approval, or the ancestor leaving the workflow ends the wait, in words from the read. A late or replayed event changes nothing Dispatch no longer shows, and a failed read retries on the outbox's backoff without holding the ancestor's own event.\n- An ancestor's `sign_off` and `close_root` wait for the roots that rest on its approval (`SIGNOFF_RESTING_ROOT_IN_WORKFLOW`) and for its open Dispatch children (`SIGNOFF_CHILD_OPEN`). Its architect gets a `resting-root` notice when such a root starts or stops resting on it.\n- No agent guide changes: AGENTS.md, every package guide and every skill are main's, which #4447 cut, and the rules this change had put there go through the tree's architect to the session coordinating that cut (dispatch://INFRA-3320/artifact/guide-rules-4447-md). The daemon's notices and the `legion` tool's `register_gate` text say what a basis takes instead of pointing into a skill.\n- A parent with an open Dispatch child starts no phase of planning through accepting. The daemon moves it to `awaiting_children` in place of that start, from a transition, from a release of a hold, or at the admission pass for a parent in `accepting`, a start not yet delivered or a worker in the middle of its phase. There it holds no admission slot, shows `in_progress`, stands in `admission.blocked` with its open children, and no role of it runs.\n- The architect gets one `awaiting-children` notice. A worker whose phase the move ended is told to push what it has and stop, and its pending task for that phase is retired. Where the move drops a merge forward that has not landed, the implementer is told of it: one that has begun the merge finishes it, pushes it and does nothing more, one that has not begun it begins none, and either merges forward later only once GitHub reads the pull request `CONFLICTING`. Any other stopped worker writes and pushes nothing more. `request_backward_move` and `sign_off` on the parent are refused `WAITING_ON_CHILDREN`.\n- Once no child is open, the admission pass returns the parent with nobody acting. A held planning or implementing start starts that phase with its task; a held test, review or acceptance comes back as the first step of the issue's walk after the implementer's, where that step stands at or before the held start (`record.ReturnStep`: `testing` on today's line), unless the pull request merged during the wait. Every task the return starts names the children that merged during the wait, with their pull requests, and raises its entry as a move back, so a completion from before the wait is refused `HANDOFF_STALE_ENTRY`. No task asks for a forward merge, and the record keeps none owed. Every testing task of a parent tells the tester to test the head merged with the tip of the pull request's base branch, in a checkout of its own that it never pushes, and to name that base commit in each result.\n- `docs/kubernetes.md` says how to roll the release back: the outbox rows and notice kinds a release before this one refuses, the move out of `awaiting_children` (it returns whether the pull request merged and which children merged), and the schema change (`children_wait_children`). Main's #5399 (dispatch://INFRA-1569) ends the hand-numbered contracts at 275 and numbers each entry at build time above it, so at this head the entry is contract 276. Before, a step that ended, registered again on the same open request and met the same Dispatch state again made the same fact id, so the read was a duplicate and the step waited for ever with nobody told (`TestTheSameReadEndsAWaitRegisteredAgainOnTheSameRequest`).\n- **R9 holds a re-admitted member in `accepting`** (M2, c4947457f7ae). `startMidPhaseMembers` judges a member in `accepting`, whose role is an architect that no phase start brings back, through `StopPromotedWorker` before it queues a start for any role. A member with an open Dispatch child moves to `awaiting_children`, gets no role back and starts no step (`TestAReadmittedMemberWithAnOpenChildComesBackWaitingOnIt`, its two `accepting` rows red before the fix).\n- **An answered request names who answered it** (Minor a, 51845928aedc). `dispatch.Ask` reads who closed an ask (`ClosedBy`): the person its answer names, or the actor its resolution names. The end of a wait says `user:alice closed approval request … as answered`, not `Someone Dispatch does not name`.\n- **The reviewer's other Minors.** b: `daemon-client.ts` names contract 276 for `register_gate`'s basis fields (7e0d9d2af9b5). c: `readBasisOnCue` holds the two cue lookups that can still run, and `pendingBasisCue` and `basisCueEvent` are unexported (51845928aedc). d: k12's exemption is read whole where the promotion reads the candidate, and only the root's walk carries it (c4947457f7ae). e: `childrenHoldingSamePhaseStart` sits beside `childrenHoldingStart` and derives its role, and `samePhaseExempt` states the merged-pull-request and accepted-entry exemption once (c4947457f7ae). f: `judgeBasisRead` calls `left()` once (51845928aedc). g: the verdict table and the left-the-workflow tests have files of their own (`gate_basis_verdict_test.go`, `gate_basis_left_root_test.go`; 51845928aedc). h: `pwDeliver` takes the issue key, and `workerTakesItsStart` is gone (7e0d9d2af9b5). i: no loop label in `startMidPhaseMembers` (c4947457f7ae). j: this body says the end names the closer, this section names 62f68c6374a7, and the slots comments of `childrenWaits` and `startsMembersThisPass` say that the return reads the slots after the pass's releases and why both reads give one answer (7e0d9d2af9b5).\n- **k11 reads the notices the daemon wrote** (8b5f9733d68c).
